submission.justification: Crystal-K3 at 4 cm thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 2.882% at 662 keV, which is optimal for the low-background screening facility. This represents a 31.7% improvement over Crystal-K1 and 67.2% improvement over Crystal-K2 at the same thickness. The systematic thickness optimization study (2-10 cm range) confirmed that 4 cm provides the best performance for K3, with resolution degrading at both smaller (3.333% at 2 cm) and larger thicknesses (2.911% at 6 cm, 4.078% at 10 cm). Crystal-K3's superior light yield (category 3) and fast decay time (category 3) make it ideal for precision gamma spectroscopy in low-background environments where energy resolution is paramount for accurately assaying construction materials for the dark-matter experiment.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 662 keV for the facility's assay programme
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 at 4 cm achieves 2.882% resolution at 662 keV, superior to K1 (4.223% at 5 cm) and K2 (8.791% at 5 cm). Thickness optimization confirmed 4 cm is optimal for K3.

requirements.requirement: The crystal must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 is one of the three evaluated candidates (K1, K2, K3) documented in the project materials.

requirements.requirement: The spectrometer must be suitable for low-background operation
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 has high light yield (category 3) and fast decay time (category 3), both critical for low-background operation to minimize pile-up and optimize signal-to-noise ratio in the low-count-rate environment of a dark-matter experiment screening facility.
Recommended thickness of 4 cm falls within the specified 2-10 cm range.
